essence.def: Essence means what God is. It is also called God’s being or substance. There is only one divine essence, and the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit each have it fully, so They are one God, not three.

nature.def: A nature is the kind of thing something is, along with everything that belongs to being that kind of thing. The divine nature includes being eternal, all-powerful and all-knowing, and human nature includes having a body and a soul. When we speak of God, “nature” means much the same as “essence”: what God is.

person.def: In speaking of God, a Person is who someone is, as distinct from what they are: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three Persons, yet one God. The word does not mean three separate beings, three parts of God, or three individuals the way three humans are; each Person is the whole one God. The Persons differ from one another only in how They are related: the Father begets, the Son is begotten, and the Spirit proceeds.

trinity.def: The Trinity is the name Christians use for the one God who exists as three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. The word itself is not found in the Bible. But it sums up what the Bible teaches: there is only one God, and the Father, the Son and the Spirit are each fully God.

eternal.def: Eternal means without beginning and without end. God has always existed and always will. He is not bound by time as we are, because He made time itself.

immutable.def: Immutable means unchanging. God does not change in His nature or His character. He does not grow, fade, or become better or worse, so He can always be trusted to be who He is.

omnipresent.def: Omnipresent means present everywhere. God is not limited by space. Yet He is not spread out with a small piece of Him in each place; He is wholly present everywhere at once.

indivisible.def: Indivisible means that God has no parts and cannot be divided. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three pieces of God, and qualities such as His love and His justice are not separate parts of Him either. This teaching is sometimes called divine simplicity.

coeternal.def: Coeternal means equally eternal. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have all existed forever. None of the Persons existed before another, and there was never a time when the Son or the Spirit did not exist.

coequal.def: Coequal means fully equal. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are equal in deity, power and glory. None is a lesser or junior God, and each is to be worshipped and honoured alike.

perichoresis.def: Perichoresis is a Greek word for the way the three Persons of the Trinity dwell in one another. Each Person is fully in the others and shares one life with Them. Yet They do not merge or lose what makes each Person distinct.

eternal-generation.def: Eternal generation describes the Son being “begotten” of the Father, the word used for how the Son comes from the Father. It has no beginning in time and involves nothing bodily: the Father did not produce the Son the way human parents have children. The Father eternally gives the whole divine essence to the Son, so this does not divide God or make a second God; the Son is fully God, one with the Father.

procession.def: Procession is the Holy Spirit’s eternal coming forth from the Father and the Son, as from one source. It is different from begetting: the Son is begotten of the Father, while the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son together, and these are two distinct ways of coming forth. It is also not the same as the Spirit being sent at Pentecost, which happened at a point in time; procession has no beginning and belongs to who the Spirit eternally is.

relations-of-origin.def: Relations of origin are what tell the three divine Persons apart. The Father begets the Son and is unbegotten, which means He comes from no one; the Son is begotten of the Father; and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son. The Persons are not set apart by different natures or ranks, since each is fully and equally the one God, but only by these relations to one another.

inseparable-operations.def: Inseparable operations means that every work God does outside Himself, such as creating, saving or giving life, is done by all three Persons together as one act. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit never work apart or split a task between Them. Yet each Person acts in His own way within that one work.

appropriation.def: Appropriation means speaking of a work that all three Persons share as belonging especially to one Person. For example, creation is often linked to the Father, redemption to the Son, and making us holy (sanctification) to the Spirit. This does not deny that the other Persons act too; it simply helps us see how each Person is fitting for that work.

incarnation.def: The Incarnation is the Son of God becoming man. Without ceasing to be God, He took a full human nature, with a real human body and a human soul. He was born as Jesus of Nazareth.

hypostatic-union.def: The hypostatic union is the joining of the divine nature and a human nature in the one Person of the Son. “Hypostatic” comes from a Greek word meaning person. The two natures are not mixed or changed into each other, and they are never divided or separated, so Jesus is one Person, truly God and truly man.
